subject: [PATCH v1 2/3] mm: memcg: read root lruvec LRU stats from the node counters

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested special casing slab stats to avoid flushing and instead read from global counters, which aligns with the patch's goal of reducing flush overhead for root memcg
sentiment_signals: default behavior should be reading node stats without flushing
reviews.raw_body:
If it's only the slab stats, it probably makes sense to special case
those instead of the rest of the readers, right? It would be nice if
the default behavior is reading the node stats that doesn't require a
flush.

2026-11-02.patch_summary: This patch series addresses the issue of memcg stats flushing, which can be costly and introduce staleness in statistics. For the root memcg, it's possible to directly read global counters instead of going through rstat, as they are always up-to-date. The patches modify various call sites to use node counters for reading LRU sizes, working set, rotation, and reclaim writeback counts. This approach reduces the number of flushes required, especially for the root memcg, which can be a performance bottleneck. The changes also improve the accuracy of statistics by reducing staleness. The series consists of three patches: one fixes the zswap shrinker's count for the root memcg, another adds a function to read node counters for the root memcg, and the third modifies DAMON's quota goals to use node counters instead of flushing.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the need to exclude certain global counters from being used as substitutes for memcg stats, citing potential issues with new stats added in the future. The author suggests either adding special casing or using a separate helper function, and is open to feedback on which approach to take.
reviews.raw_body:
If we were to special case it, it would need to exclude more than a
couple, I think. I asked a LLM and it says NR_KERNEL_STACK_KB,
NR_PAGETABLE, NR_SECONDARY_PAGETABLE, NR_VMALLOC, NR_HUGETLB,
WORKINGSET_NODERECLAIM would also need to be excluded. We could add
this special casing in, but we would need to make sure any new stat
that gets added in the future that belongs on the exclusion list gets
put on it. If it's missed, the failure would be silent whereas with a
separate helper, callers have to explicitly opt in. I'm happy to go
either way though, so if there's one way you prefer, I'm happy to do
that for v2.

Thanks,
Joanne

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary:
The reviewer questioned whether it's intentional that the patch distinguishes between 'root' and 'node' stats in memory.stat, suggesting a potential inconsistency across various statistics.

Reviewer Yosry Ahmed questioned whether the distinction between root memcg stats and node stats is intentional, suggesting that the default behavior should be to use node stats (majority behavior) unless explicitly opted out, and requested input from the memcg community.
reviews.raw_body:
Interesting. So for all these stats, root memcg stats (from
memory.stat) is not the same as the node stat? They all draw a
distinction between "accounted to root" vs "not accounted"? I wonder
if this is intentional for all of them.

---

I think we probably want to first understand if these stats are
supposed to be different between the root memcg stats and the node
stats first. Personally, I think the default should be the majority
behavior, which I think is that node stats and root memcg stats are
the same, so I am leaning toward explicit opt-out. Let's also see what
memcg folks think.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary:
Author Joanne Koong addressed a concern about kernel memory accounting for allocations made by tasks running in the root cgroup, explaining that it was intentionally designed to avoid extra overhead costs and proposing an alternative approach of reading node counters instead of going through rstat.

Author agrees that the feedback is reasonable and asks for input from other memcg developers.
sentiment_signals: author agreed to consider the feedback
reviews.raw_body:
I think there's 2 categories:
a) the allocation isn't acccounted to any memcg (eg kernel page
tables, hugetlb when hugetlb accounting is off, unaccounted slab
caches and kmallocs w/out __GFP_ACCOUNT, and most vmalloc). These
values only get added to the node counter

b) the allocation is accounted, but it comes from a task running in
the root cgroup (eg kernel stacks, user + secondary page tables,
accounted slab, etc)

I think a) has to stay as is since it's not linked to any memcg. For
b), it seems intentional from the original commit that added kernel
memory accounting logic (commit 7ae1e1d0f8ac ("memcg: kmem controller
infrastructure")). The commit message for that explicitly says
tracking kernel memory pages to a given memcg "will happen whenever
the caller includes the flag __GFP_KMEMCG flag and the task belongs to
a memcg other than the root". (__GFP_KMEMCG later became
__GFP_ACCOUNT). I wonder though if this was to avoid extra overhead
costs (eg for systems that don't use cgroups) on the hot paths, since
it would need to do non-trivial per-object work. If root read the node
counters for the stats that are in category b (excluding the stats
that are in both category a and b) instead of going through rstat
(which is what this series does for the LRU stats), there wouldn't
need to be any extra overhead at allocation time, since nothing would
need to be tracked.

---

That seems reasonable to me. memcg folks, do you have any thoughts on this?

Thanks,
Joanne
